normalization_finding.what: config/model-lane-assignment.json carries two identities: the tracked bytes are LF (sha256 206ec9b8...) and a Windows checkout materialises CRLF (sha256 8ac81357...). The epoch-41 registry pins the CRLF digest 8ac81357 and main's registry pins cfbff111, which matches NEITHER of its own assignment's digests.
normalization_finding.why_it_matters: a digest pin taken over a working-tree normalisation only holds on the host that wrote it; a Linux CI checkout would compute the LF digest and read a false drift
normalization_finding.action_taken: the port records both digests (source_of_routes.sha256 = CRLF twin inherited from the branch, source_of_routes.sha256_lf = the tracked bytes) and the validator accepts either; no pin was silently reconciled
normalization_finding.main_pin_verdict: main's own pin cfbff111 is stale and matches no digest of its own projection
